title: fix(mcp): accept grouped frames in strict stdio clients
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a strict MCP subprocess connection closes when several valid messages arrive together and their combined stdout chunk exceeds the per-message limit.

## User Impact

The strict MCP client used by the CUA adapter and plugin SDK accepts individually bounded messages regardless of how the pipe groups them. Oversized messages still retire the connection; the configured limit includes the terminating newline.

## Why This Change Was Made

The inherited check counted the entire incoming chunk against one frame. The decoder now validates each frame before retaining the chunk, preserving pending bytes if any complete or partial frame is too large. Ordinary chunks that fit still take the existing fast path. The SDK's separate default stdio buffer and its limit are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Exact-head [CI run 35817718681](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35817718681) passed on `8d51924c4655a5e0b744496d0aa41b7c17616575`: 132 successful jobs, 17 skipped, zero failures. ClawSweeper reviewed this head with no findings and accepted the real subprocess proof.
- Two decoder cases and the strict-client regression fail on the original code and pass after the repair. All 19 focused tests pass, covering combined messages, fragmented input, oversized later frames, atomic rejection, UTF-8, protocol validation and connection retirement.
- A real local MCP subprocess emits two legal messages in one write. Before the repair, the client reports the line-size error and becomes unavailable. Afterward, the observed 1,553-byte read succeeds with a 1,024-byte per-message limit. An oversized-message control still fails on an observed 1,953-byte read. Both runs await owned-process cleanup. This uses a synthetic server over real processes and pipes, not a mock transport or the native CUA driver.
- An independent public HTTP smoke test used the supported CLI with isolated config/state against DeepWiki: add, status and probe succeeded, discovering three server tools and seven projected tools with no diagnostics. This checks the separate HTTP flow, not the strict decoder.
- Measured one-worker command walls: decoder 14 tests in 1.95 seconds; client 5 tests in 23.14 seconds, mostly worker preparation/import cost. Test bodies use existing fixtures and no new process boots, sleeps or polling. In exact-head CI, the summed rounded case durations were 2 ms for the 14 decoder cases and 158 ms for the five client cases. Their covering jobs took 375 and 473 seconds, including other files and setup; standalone CI file wall times were unavailable.
- Diff-scoped deslop and independent P2 review found no actionable findings. The first type check caught unsafe indexing in the new test fixture; named typed fixture values now preserve the same byte cases. One cost run collected no tests because a concurrent CLI build changed generated artifacts during compilation; after those builds joined, the measured runs passed.
- Final selected changed-file checks passed, including production/test types, scoped lint, formatting, dead-export scans and import-cycle guards.
